definition: In natural language processing, textual entailment (TE), also known as natural language inference (NLI), is a directional relation between text fragments.
details: The relation holds whenever the truth of one text fragment follows from another text.
story: Picture a translator at the United Nations, listening to one language and whispering the meaning into another in real time. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. Meaning lives in company — a word is known by the words it keeps. That pattern-earned fluency is Textual entailment.
